title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex, a crystalline-cohomology setting. Grothendieck is building a de Rham-type complex from auxiliary data. He considers 'admissible theories', bigraded complexes C^{**}_α, subject to two technical conditions: being a 'quasi-resolution' of S_n (probably a symmetric or divided-power functor; unsure) and being 'quasi-flasque'.

He observes that every morphism in the category of admissible objects is already a quasi-isomorphism, meaning it induces isomorphisms on Tor / homology. So the natural step is to localize at all morphisms. The category of fractions inverting everything is the groupoid generated by the admissible category, i.e. its fundamental groupoid.

The goal is to show this groupoid is connected and simply connected. Equivalently, any two admissible choices are linked by an isomorphism in the localization, and that isomorphism is unique. This says the resulting invariant is canonically independent of the auxiliary choice, up to unique isomorphism.

To get this, he writes down the two axioms of a cofiltered category:
(a) for any two admissible C, C' there is an admissible C'' with maps to both;
(b) for any two parallel maps C' ⇉ C there is a map C'' → C' that equalizes them.

A non-empty cofiltered category has contractible nerve. In particular, inverting all its arrows gives a trivial (connected, simply connected) groupoid. These axioms are also of calculus-of-fractions type.

Grothendieck hesitates over which side the calculus of fractions should be on. The main text says 'à gauche'; the right margin says 'il y aurait plus de chances avec calcul de fractions à droite ???'. A large question mark in the left margin flags the whole criterion as unverified. The NB in brackets, mentioning 'cohérents' and B_K = k{B}, is too illegible to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical error. The criterion is correct provided the category is non-empty: a cofiltered category localized at all morphisms is equivalent to the point. Note also that (a) and (b) give cofilteredness, which is stronger than needed. Connectedness plus simple connectedness of the nerve would suffice.

The left/right labelling of the calculus of fractions is uncertain in the text itself, as the margin shows. This reflects the usual convention ambiguity (Gabriel–Zisman versus later usage), not an actual error.
Whether admissible theories actually satisfy (a) and (b) is not shown on this page; the page leaves it open.

ideas.what: Invert all morphisms of a category of auxiliary 'admissible' resolutions and ask that the resulting groupoid be connected and simply connected, i.e. canonical independence of choices up to unique isomorphism.
ideas.modern_name: Contractible (or 1-connected) category of choices; localization / fundamental groupoid of a category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard homotopical-algebra philosophy (Gabriel–Zisman 1967; Quillen 1973 Theorem A circle of ideas)
ideas.where_published: Theme pervasive in Pursuing Stacks (asphericity, categories of choices); filtered-category techniques in SGA 4 Exposé I

ideas.what: Criterion via cofilteredness: (a) a common refinement of two admissible objects exists; (b) parallel arrows can be equalized.
ideas.modern_name: Cofiltered category ⇒ contractible nerve / trivial groupoid of fractions

ideas.what: Admissible bicomplexes as 'quasi-resolutions' of S_n that are 'quasi-flasque', all of whose morphisms are Tor-quasi-isomorphisms; auxiliary data for the divided-power de Rham construction.
ideas.modern_name: Category of resolutions / acyclic models used to define a canonical complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Acyclic models (Eilenberg–Mac Lane); in the crystalline setting, Illusie and Berthelot

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working step: making a construction independent of auxiliary choices by showing the indexing category is cofiltered. The only personal touch is the left/right fractions hesitation. Nothing here appears new to the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Cal. signification des Cong ?' is doubtful. It is plausibly 'Cela signifie...' or an abbreviation such as 'Cofilt.?' (cofiltrant), since conditions (a) and (b) that follow are exactly the cofiltered axioms.
Line 2: 'résolution de S_n' fits the image ('quasi' in quotes before 'résolution').
Bracketed NB: the image shows 'NB rappelons que ceci ... [cohérents inserted above] ... B_K = k{B}'. The middle words are largely illegible; the transcription's [?] markers are appropriate.
Right margin reads: 'il y aurait plus de chances avec calcul de fractions à droite ???'. The transcription is correct.
The second-to-last displayed arrow points C''^{**}_α → C'^{**}_α, with 'qui "égalise"' below it. The transcription is correct.
